tasks.title: Confirm VariantType enum vs string in backend report.py, report to Vansh
tasks.description:
sagar, this is a quick one but it gates the adapter design, so it can't stay unknown. it came out of vansh's report-format compatibility check (the doc mapping the vmis json against the gg report schema): https://github.com/GGinc/gg-vmis/blob/main/docs/vmis/REPORT_FORMAT_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK.md (section 7, Q3 and remaining items). vansh couldn't answer it himself because the file in question lives in the backend repo, not the frontend one he reviewed.

the problem in plain terms: in g551d_base.json our variant_type value is "missense_variant". the backend report schema app/schemas/report.py has a field called VariantType. if VariantType is a strict pydantic enum (only accepts a fixed set like SNV/indel), then handing it "missense_variant" makes the report-generation call throw a validation error and the report never renders. if VariantType is just a free-text string, "missense_variant" passes fine and there's nothing to fix. nobody has actually looked, so we're designing the adapter on a guess.

what to actually do: open app/schemas/report.py in the backend repo, read the VariantType definition, and answer one question, is it a strict enum or a free string. then tell
 if strict enum: the adapter must convert/derive the SNV/indel class from ref/alt allele lengths before sending, and keep the VEP consequence (missense_variant) in molecular_consequence. the json already separates molecular_consequence from variant_type exactly so this conversion is possible, so this would just confirm the adapter design is right.
 if free string: no conversion needed, adapter passes it straight through.

done = you've read report.py, posted "enum" or "string" here (paste the VariantType definition if you can), and vansh has what he needs to finalize the adapter.

What must be true before this is marked complete

1. The mechanism is correct and sourced
 Primary mechanism is the reduced-function gating defect (Class III), with defective trafficking explicitly rejected and reduced stability noted as a secondary hypothesis
 Every factual claim carries a PMID or DOI — no uncited assertions. The graph-write gate rejects any factual edge missing source + evidence_label + retrieval_date
 Established facts, inferences, and research hypotheses are clearly separated and labeled
 Confidence levels are justified by the evidence behind them, not asserted

2. The variant identifiers are pinned and verified
 Gene: CFTR (HGNC:1884)
 Transcript: NM_000492.4 (MANE Select), protein NP_000483.3
 Coding: c.1652G>A — Protein: p.(Gly551Asp) / G551D
 ClinVar: VCV000007120, Pathogenic, 4-star practice guideline (NOT the case-pack's VCV000007105, which was wrong and is flagged for correction)

 Research-use-only banner present; no diagnosis, prescribing, dosing, or "will work" language anywhere
 Any therapeutic mention (e.g. ivacaftor as a mechanism-matched potentiator) is framed as a research hypothesis with verified DailyMed status, never as a treatment recommendation
 Contradictions are preserved as explicit objects, never silently harmonized

5. It is demonstrable
 The cited mechanism note populates the shared VMIS JSON, the mechanism graph, the phenotype explanation, and the exportable RUO report
 Reviewer (Zuhra) selects a final outcome using the VMIS scientific review checklist: Approved / Approved with revisions / Requires additional evidence / Rejected / Deferred

REVIEWER INTRODUCTION

Thank you for reviewing this demonstration. A few things to set context before you begin:

VMIS (Variant-to-Mechanism Intelligence System) takes a single confirmed pathogenic variant and reconstructs the chain from the variant to its molecular mechanism, to the affected pathway and cellular consequence, to the patient phenotype, and finally to mechanism-matched research hypotheses. It explains why a variant is pathogenic, not just that it is.

CFTR G551D is our first demonstration case. You are looking at one variant, one transcript, end to end.

This system is research-use-only. It does not provide diagnosis, prescribing, dosing, or treatment recommendations, and we are not asking you to make any clinical judgment.

What we are asking you to evaluate is clarity, scientific defensibility, and usefulness — whether the explanation holds up, whether the evidence is verifiable, and whether this would be useful in your work.
